What brings understanding is love. When your heart is full, then you will listen to the teacher, to the beggar, to the laughter of children, to the rainbow, and to the sorrow of man. Under every stone and leaf, that which is eternal exists.
quotes.source: "Ninth Talk in Bombay, (14 March 1948), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. BO48Q1, published in The Collected Works, Vol. IV, p. 200

quotes.text: Silence is difficult and arduous, it is not to be played with. It isn't something that you can experience by reading a book, or by listening to a talk, or by sitting together, or by retiring into a wood or a monastery.
quotes.source: Sixth talk in London (17 June 1962), published in The Collected Works of J. Krishnamurti : Vol. XIII, 1962-1963: A Psychological Revoluti…

quotes.text: Thought is matter as much as the floor, the wall, the telephone, are matter. Energy functioning in a pattern becomes matter. That is all life is … Matter and energy are interrelated.

The whole of Asia believes in reincarnation, in being reborn in another life. When you enquire what it is that is going to be born in the next life, you come up against difficulties. What is it? Yourself? What are you?
quotes.source: 6th Public Talk, Saanen (28 July 1970) 'The Mechanical Activity of Thought" in The Impossible Question (1972) Part I, Ch. 6

quotes.text: How is the mind which functions on knowledge — how is the brain which is recording all the time — to end, to see the importance of recording and not let it move in any other direction?
quotes.source: 1970s, A Wholly Different Way of Living (1970), p. 19

quotes.text: The brain is the source of thought. The brain is matter and thought is matter. Can the brain — with all its reactions and its immediate responses to every challenge and demand — can the brain be very still?
A mind that is in meditation is concerned only with meditation, not with the meditator.
quotes.source: The First Step is the Last Step (2004), p. 281

quotes.text: Life as we live it is obviously very brutal, and makes us insensitive, dull, heavy, stupid, and so we may hope through ideas,through ideational mentation, to bring about a certain quality of sensitivity.
quotes.source: 1970s, The Awakening of Intelligence (1973), Part V, Ch. 3 : 3rd Public Talk Madras 14th January 1968 "The Sacred"

quotes.text: Meditation is the emptying of the mind of all thought, for thought and feeling dissipate energy. They are repetitive, producing mechanical activities which are a necessary part of existence.
It is man’s pretence that because he has choice he is free. Freedom is pure observation without direction, without fear of punishment and reward.
The very nature of intelligence is sensitivity, and this sensitivity is love. Without this intelligence there can be no compassion.
quotes.source: 1980s, Letters to the Schools (1981, 1985), Vol. I, p. 113

quotes.text: First, we must be very clear that you and the speaker are treating life not as a problem but as a tremendous movement. If your brain is trained to solve problems, then you will treat this movement as a problem to be solved.
Are we wasting our lives? By that word “wasting” we mean dissipating our energy in various ways, dissipating it in specialized professions. Are we wasting our whole existence, our life?
quotes.source: 1980s, That Benediction is Where You Are (1985), p. 63

quotes.text: Insight is not a matter of memory, of knowledge and time, which are all thought. So I would say insight is the total absence of the whole movement of thought as time and remembrance. So there is direct perception.
quotes.source: Questioning Krishnamurti : J. Krishnamurti in dialogue (1996), p. 165

quotes.text: The answer is in the problem, not away from the problem. I go through the searching, analysing, dissecting process, in order to escape from the problem.
quotes.source: "Eighth Talk in The Oak Grove, 7 August 1949", J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. 490807, Vol. V, p. 283

quotes.text: Superstition is another mighty evil, and has caused much terrible cruelty. The man who is a slave to it despises others who are wiser, tries to force them to do as he does.
quotes.source: At the Feet of the Master (1911), § IV

quotes.text: Your prejudices, your fears, your authorities, your churches new and old – all these, I maintain, are a barrier to understanding. I cannot make myself clearer than this.
So, a man who is really earnest must begin with himself, he must be passively aware of all his thoughts, feelings and actions. Again, this is not a matter of time. There is no end to self-knowledge.
quotes.source: New Delhi India 1st Public Talk (14 November 1948)

quotes.text: Learning in the true sense of the word is possible only in that state of attention, in which there is no outer or inner compulsion. Right thinking can come about only when the mind is not enslaved by tradition and memory.
quotes.source: "Life Ahead: On Learning and the Search for Meaning" (1963), Introduction, J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. 261, p. 13, 2005 edition

quotes.text: For centuries we have been spoon-fed by our teachers, by our authorities, by our books, our saints. We say, "Tell me all about it — what lies beyond the hills and the mountains and the earth?"
Do you decide to observe? Or do you merely observe? Do you decide and say, "I am going to observe and learn"? For then there is the question: "Who is deciding?" Is it will that says, "I must"?
quotes.source: 5th Public Talk Saanen (26th July 1970); also in "Fear and Pleasure", The Collected Works, Vol. X

quotes.text: How can one be free of the images that one has? First of all, I must find out how these images come into being, what is the mechanism that creates them.

When man becomes aware of the movement of his own thoughts, he will see the division between the thinker and thought, the observer and the observed, the experiencer and the experience. He will discover that this division is an illusion.

Attention involves seeing and hearing. We hear not only with our ears but also we are sensitive to the tones, the voice, to the implication of words, to hear without interference, to capture instantly the depth of a sound.
quotes.source: 1980s, Letters to the Schools (1981, 1985), Vol. II, p. 30

quotes.text: You cannot find truth through anybody else. How can you? Surely, truth is not something static; it has no fixed abode; it is not an end, a goal. On the contrary, it is living, dynamic, alert, alive. How can it be an end?
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. VI, p 5, "First Talk in Rajahmundry (20 November 1949), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Ser…

quotes.text: You know, in the case of most of us, the mind is noisy, everlastingly chattering to itself , soliloquizing or chattering about something, or trying to talk to itself, to convince itself of something; it is always moving, noisy.

The world accepts and follows the traditional approach. The primary cause of disorder in ourselves is the seeking of reality promised by another; we mechanically follow somebody who will assure us a comfortable spiritual life.

Fear is always in relation to something; it does not exist by itself. There is fear of what happened yesterday in relation to the possibility of its repetition tomorrow; there is always a fixed point from which relationship takes place.

And the brain has been trained to record because then in that recording there is safety, there is security, there is strength, a vitality, and therefore in that recording the mind creates the image about oneself. Right?
quotes.source: 2nd Question and Answer Session, Saanen (24 July 1980), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. SA80Q2

quotes.text: Attention is this hearing and this seeing, and this attention has no limitation, no resistance, so it is limitless. To attend implies this vast energy: it is not pinned down to a point.
quotes.source: 1980s, Letters to the Schools (1981, 1985), Vol. II, p. 31

quotes.text: Truth is not something in the distance; there is no path to it, there is neither your path nor my path; there is no devotional path, there is no path of knowledge or path of action, because truth has no path to it.
quotes.source: "Fifth Talk in Bombay 1950 (12 March 1950), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. 500312, The Collected Works, Vol. VI, p. 134

quotes.text: You know, actually we have no love — that is a terrible thing to realize. Actually we have no love; we have sentiment; we have emotionality, sensuality, sexuality; we have remembrances of something which we have thought as love.
quotes.source: Varanasi 5th Public Talk (28 November 1964), The Collected Works, Vol. XV

quotes.text: That is the first thing to learn — not to seek. When you seek you are really only window-shopping.

Now, one sees all that by observing, by being aware, watching, one is aware of all this. Then out of that awareness you see there is no division between the observer and the observed. It is a trick of thought which demands security.
The understanding of relationship, fear, pleasure and sorrow is to bring order in our house. Without order you cannot possibly meditate.
quotes.source: The Network of Thought (1982) J.Krishnamurti Online. Serial No. 332. , p. 96

quotes.text: Meditation is not a process of learning how to meditate; it is the very inquiry into what is meditation.
quotes.source: "Third Talk at Rajghat" (25 December 1955), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. 551225, Vol. IX, p. 192

quotes.text: Throughout life, from childhood, from school until we die, we are taught to compare ourselves with another; yet when I compare myself with another I am destroying myself.

I think there is a difference between the human being and the individual. The individual is a local entity, living in a particular country, belonging to a particular culture, particular society, particular religion.
It is utterly and irrevocably possible to empty all hurts and, therefore, to love, to have compassion.

The questioner says, how can the conditioned brain grasp the unlimited, which is beauty, love, and truth? What is the ground of compassion and intelligence, and can it come upon us — each one of us? Are you inviting compassion?
Please let us be clear on this point — that you cannot by any process, through any discipline, through any form of meditation, go to truth, God, or whatever name you like to give it.
quotes.source: Second Talk in Poona (10 September 1958), J.Krishnamurti Online, JKO Serial No. 580910, Vol. XI, p. 20

quotes.text: We need tremendous energy to bring about a psychological change in ourselves as human beings, because we have lived far too long in a world of make-belief, in a world of brutality, violence, despair, anxiety.
quotes.source: Talks in Europe 1968, 5th Public Talk, Amsterdam, The Netherlands (22 May 1968) Collected Works, Vol. XV

quotes.text: We human beings are what we have been for millions of years — colossally greedy, envious, aggressive, jealous, anxious and despairing, with occasional flashes of joy and affection.
Goodness is not the pursuit of conformity. If you conform to a belief, to a concept, to an idea, to a principle, that is not good, because it creates conflict.
quotes.source: First Public Talk at Ojai (7 April 1979) published in This Light in Oneself : True Meditation (1999), edited by Ray McCoy, p. 12

quotes.text: Desire, which has been the driving force in man, has created a great many pleasant and useful things; desire also, in man's relationships, has created a great many problems and turmoil and misery — the desire for pleasure.
quotes.source: Krishnamurti to Himself (1987) - 1993 edition; J.Krishnamurti Online. Serial No. 60039

quotes.text: I think we must see this very clearly right at the beginning — that if one would solve the everyday problems of existence, whatever they may be, one must first see the wider issues and then come to the detail.
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XI, p. 62

quotes.text: Can't you fall in love and not have a possessive relationship? I love someone and she loves me and we get married — that is all perfectly straightforward and simple, in that there is no conflict at all.
quotes.source: 'Krishnamurti Foundation Trust Bulletin 3 (1969), and Krishnamurti Foundation Trust Bulletin 4, (1969)

quotes.text: We are afraid of the known and afraid of the unknown. That is our daily life and in that there is no hope, and therefore every form of philosophy, every form of theological concept, is merely an escape from the actual reality of what is.
When death comes, it does not ask your permission; it comes and takes you; it destroys you on the spot.
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XI, p. 242

quotes.text: What can a human being do — what can you and I do — to create a completely different society? We are asking ourselves a very serious question. Is there anything to be done at all? What can we do? Will somebody tell us? People have told us.

We know only fragmentarily this extraordinary thing called life; we have never looked at sorrow, except through the screen of escapes; we have never seen the beauty, the immensity of death, and we know it only through fear and sadness.
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XI, p. 288

quotes.text: You cannot depend upon anybody. There is no guide, no teacher, no authority. There is only you — your relationship with others and with the world — there is nothing else.
Passion is something which very few of us have really felt. What we may have felt is enthusiasm, which is being caught up in an emotional state over something.
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XIII, p. 251

quotes.text: It is important to understand from the very beginning that I am not formulating any philosophy or any theological structure of ideas or theological concepts. It seems to me that all ideologies are utterly idiotic.
Just observe what you are. What you are is the fact: the fact that you are jealous, anxious, envious, brutal, demanding, violent. That is what you are.
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XIV, p. 301

quotes.text: Attention is not concentration. When you concentrate, as most people try to do — what takes place when you are concentrating?
quotes.source: Posthumous publications, The Collected Works, Vol. XV, p. 321

quotes.text: You know, I think everybody longs to be loved, and longs to know that he or she is lovable. And, consequently, the greatest thing that we can do is to help somebody know that they're loved and capable of loving.
quotes.source: Fred Rogers: America's Favorite Neighbor (television documentary), 2003.

quotes.text: Yes, when I was here the first word of the alma mater was 'Men…Men of Dartmouth, give a rouse…' Well, now the first word is 'Dear.' Some things change for the better.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Dartmouth College June 9th, 2002

quotes.text: Our world hangs like a magnificent jewel in the vastness of space. Every one of us is a part of that jewel. A facet of that jewel. And in the perspective of infinity, our differences are infinitesimal.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Dartmouth College June 9th, 2002

quotes.text: I believe that appreciation is a holy thing, that when we look for what's best in the person we happen to be with at the moment, we're doing what God does; so in appreciating our neighbor, we're participating in something truly sacred.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: Vermont is a small state which makes an enormous difference.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: It's not the honors and the prizes and the fancy outsides of life which ultimately nourish our souls. It's the knowing that we can be trusted, that we never have to fear the truth, that the bedrock of our very being is good stuff.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: It's our insides that make us who we are, that allow us to dream and wonder and feel for others. That's what's essential. That's what will always make the biggest difference in our world.
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: Little by little we human beings are confronted with situations that give us more and more clues that we aren't perfect.
quotes.source: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Thoughts For All Ages

quotes.text: If only you could sense how important you are to the lives of those you meet; how important you can be to people you may never even dream of. There is something of yourself that you leave at every meeting with another person.
quotes.source: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Thoughts For All Ages

quotes.text: Fame is a four letter word and like tape, or zoom, or face, or pain, or life, or love, what ultimately matters is what we do with it.
quotes.source: When introduced to the TV Hall of Fame

quotes.text: Children are to be respected and I respect them deeply. They've taught me an awful lot.
quotes.source: Interviewed by Joan Rivers on The Tonight Show (1983)

quotes.text: Very frankly, I am opposed to people being programmed by others. My whole approach in broadcasting has always been 'You are an important person just the way you are. You can make healthy decisions.

This is what I give. I give an expression of care every day to each child, to help him realize that he is unique. I end the program by saying, 'You've made this day a special day, by just your being you.
quotes.source: Testimony before U.S. Senate committee, May 1, 1969. Featured in Fred Rogers: America's Favorite Neighbor (television documentary), 2003.

quotes.text: Well, what is essential about you? And who are those who have helped you become the person that you are?
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Dartmouth College June 9th, 2002 and Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: When I say it's you I like, I'm talking about that part of you that knows that life is far more than anything you can ever see or hear or touch.
quotes.source: Source Commencement Address at Dartmouth College June 9th, 2002

quotes.text: As human beings, our job in life is to help people realize how rare and valuable each one of us really is, that each of us has something that no one else has—or ever will have—something inside that is unique to all time.
quotes.source: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Thoughts For All Ages

quotes.text: Both Joanne and I can recall many times when we wish we'd said or done something different. But we didn't, and we've learned not to feel too guilty about that.
quotes.source: Foreword of Many Ways to Say I Love You

quotes.text: I am not a man of etiquette, I don't know manners. I simply call a spade a fucking spade, because that's what it is.
Jesus is a rebel, just as Buddha or Lao Tzu is. When the church starts establishing itself it starts destroying the rebelliousness of Jesus, Buddha, because rebellion cannot go with an establishment.
Don't say this is good and that is bad. Drop all discrimination. Accept everything as it is.
Man has nothing else to do but surrender — in deep trust, in deep love. Don’t be a doer, just surrender. Let there be a let-go.
quotes.source: The Art of Dying (osho.com; retrieved August 2012), Chapter 6, 14.

quotes.text: If you believe in any religion you cannot meditate. Religion is an interference in your meditation. Meditation needs no God, no heaven, no hell, no fear of punishment, and no allurement of pleasure.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 10

quotes.text: All the Buddhas of all the ages have been telling you a very simple fact: Be — don't try to become. Within these two words — being and becoming, your whole life is contained. Being is enlightenment, becoming is ignorance.
The Christian priest is not interested in God: he is interested in creating a business. He has to claim that Jesus is the only way, that all other ways are wrong. He is in search of customers.
Liberation cannot be desired because desire is the bondage. When you are desireless, you are liberated.
You say that in heaven there is eternal beauty. The eternal beauty is here and now, not in heaven.
Tantra accepts everything, lives everything. That's why tantra never could become a very accepted ideology. It always remained a fringe ideology.
Democracy basically means government by the people, of the people, for the people; but the people are retarded. So let us say government by the retarded, for the retarded, of the retarded.
quotes.source: Is Democracy the Best Way of Government? (1981) YouTube video of the lecture

quotes.text: Tantra is a great yea-sayer; it says yes to everything.
Tantra says there is nobody above you whom you have to follow, through whom you have to get your pattern.
The ordinary society is like a paperweight on you: it won't allow you to fly.
The tantra masters are simply wild flowers, they have everything in them.
When you are no more, only then for the first time will you be.

One has to reach to the absolute state of awareness: that is Zen. You cannot do it every morning for a few minutes or for half an hour and then forget all about it. It has to become like your heartbeat.
quotes.source: Walking in Zen, Sitting in Zen (1982)

quotes.text: The first thing to be understood about a man like Jesus is that whatsoever the church that is bound to grow around such a man says about him, it is bound to be wrong. What the Christian church says about Christ cannot be true.

Just before twenty-first March, 1953, seven days before, I stopped working on myself. A moment comes when you see the whole futility of effort. You have done all that you can do and nothing is happening.

Find moments when you are not, and those will be the moments when you will be for the first time...really. So I am the white cloud, and the whole effort is to make you also white clouds drifting in the sky.
quotes.source: My Way: The Way of the White Clouds (1995)

quotes.text: And my grandparents became very aware of one thing—that I enjoyed my aloneness. They had seen that I had no desire to go to the village to meet anybody, or to talk with anybody.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 6

quotes.text: I would like that what I am doing is not lost. So I am trying in every possible way to drop all those things which in the past have been barriers for the revolution to continue and grow.
quotes.source: The Last Testament : Interviews with the World Press (1986)

quotes.text: Near about twelve my eyes suddenly opened — I had not opened them. The sleep was broken by something else. I felt a great presence around me in the room. It was a very small room.
Look for the mysterious in life. Wherever you look — in the white clouds, in the stars in the night, in the flowers, in a flowing river — wherever you look, look for the mystery.
quotes.source: My Way: The Way of the White Clouds (1995)

quotes.text: For seven years I remained undisturbed—no one to nag me, to prepare me for the world of business, politics, diplomacy. My grandparents were more interested in leaving me as natural as possible—particularly my grandmother.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 7

quotes.text: Buddha declared before his death that he would be coming again after twenty-five centuries, and that his name would be Maitreya. Maitreya means the friend.
quotes.source: The Last Testament : Interviews with the World Press (1986)

quotes.text: Only a ripe fruit falls to the ground. Ripeness is all. An unripe ego cannot be thrown, cannot be destroyed. And if you struggle with an unripe ego to destroy and dissolve it, the whole effort is going to be a failure.
quotes.source: My Way: The Way of the White Clouds (1995)

quotes.text: Nobody should lie — to a child, at least — it is unforgivable. Children have been exploited for centuries just because they are willing to trust. You can lie to them very easily and they will trust you.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 13

quotes.text: I have never been a celibate. If people believe so, that is their foolishness. I have always loved women — and perhaps more women than anybody else.
quotes.source: The Last Testament : Interviews with the World Press (1986)

quotes.text: The so-called mahatmas and saints are all cowards. I have never come across a single mahatma—Hindu, Mohammedan, Christian, Buddhist—who can be said to be really a rebellious spirit.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 19

quotes.text: It was good of Friedrich Nietzsche to declare God dead — I declare that he has never been born. It is a created fiction, an invention, not a discovery. Do you understand the difference between invention and discovery?
quotes.source: God is Dead, Now Zen is the Only Living Truth (1989) YouTube video of the lecture

quotes.text: My grandfather ... had raised me with absolute freedom, no inhibitions, no suppressions, and no commandments.Love with freedom—if you have it, you are a king or a queen. That is the real kingdom of God—love with freedom.
quotes.source: Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), p. 25

quotes.text: I believe and trust absolutely in existence. If there is any truth in what I am saying, it will survive.

Just a few days ago a man came to see me and he said, "I am a humble man. I am just like the dust on your feet. I have been trying for almost twenty years to achieve higher consciousness, but I have been a failure. Why can't I attain?"
quotes.source: Just Like That: Talks on Sufism (1993)

quotes.text: Tao mystics never talk about God, reincarnation, heaven, hell. No, they don't talk about these things. These are all creations of human mind: explanations for something which can never be explained, explanations for the mystery.

It is not decided by votes what is true; otherwise we could never come to any truth, ever. People will vote for what is comfortable — and lies are very comfortable because you don't have to do anything about them, you just have to believe.
Whenever I meet prostitutes, they never speak of sex. They inquire about the soul, and about God. I also meet many ascetics and monks, and whenever we are alone they ask about nothing but sex.
Nobody can teach you love. Love you have to find yourself, within your being, by raising your consciousness to higher levels. And when love comes, there is no question of responsibility.

Any mundane activity can become meditative. Digging a hole in the garden, planting new roses in the garden — you can do it with such tremendous love and compassion, you can do it with the hands of a buddha.
I do not ordinarily make prophecies, but about this I am absolutely prophetic: the coming hundred years are going to be more and more irrational, and more and more mystical.
My whole teaching consists of two words, meditation and love. Meditate so that you can feel immense silence, and love so that your life can become a song, a dance, a celebration.
Ecstasy is our very nature, not to be ecstatic is simply unnecessary. To be ecstatic is natural, spontaneous. It needs no effort to be ecstatic, it needs great effort to be miserable.

Remain in wonder if you want mysteries to open up for you. Mysteries never open up for those who go on questioning. Questioners sooner or later end up in a library. They end up with scriptures, because scriptures are full of answers.
The longer a person has been dead the greater is the tradition … If Buddha is alive you can barely tolerate him.
When I am gone I hope there may still be courageous people in the world to criticize me, so that I don't become a hindrance on anybody's path.

You must have heard about the beautiful Sufi legend of Majnu and Laila. It is not an ordinary love story. The word majnu means mad, mad for God. And laila is the symbol of God. Sufis think of God as the beloved; laila means the beloved.
quotes.source: Sufis, The People of the Path, Vol. 1

quotes.text: Nature has come to a point where now, unless you take individual responsibility, you cannot grow. More than this nature cannot do. It has done enough.

If you really want to know who I am, you have to be as absolutely empty as I am. Then two mirrors will be facing each other, and only emptiness will be mirrored. Infinite emptiness will be mirrored: two mirrors facing each other.
quotes.source: Come Follow To You, Vol. 2, Chapter 4; in Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic (2000), Part 2.

quotes.text: I help people as a way to work on myself, and I work on myself to help people… To me, that’s what the emerging game is all about.
quotes.source: As quoted in "Baba Ram Dass in the realm of Visionary Artist Martina Hoffmann: in the end there’s only one spirit and one humanness", by…

quotes.text: Only when I know who I am will I know what is possible.
There are three stages in this journey that I have been on. The first. the social science stage; the second, the psychedelic stage; and the third, the yogi stage.
I learned more in the six or seven hours of this experience than I had learned in all my years as a psychologist.
quotes.source: (quoting Timothy Leary's description of the Psilocybin experience).

quotes.text: I'd get to a point with my colleagues when I couldn't explain any further, because it came down to "To him who has had the experience no explanation is necessary, to him who has not, none is possible.".
We were exploring this inner realm of consciousness that we had been theorizing about all these years and suddenly we were traveling in and through and around it.

It would be best not to impose a model too soon, because the model that exists in the west for these states is pathological, and the model that exists in the primitive cultures is mystical and religious.
quotes.source: (quoting Timothy Leary's description of the Psilocybin experience).

quotes.text: Whenever anybody that I trusted brought along some new chemical, I would open my mouth and off I'd go.
I had plenty of LSD, but why take it. I knew what it was going to do, what it was going to tell me. It was going to show me that garden again and then I was going to be cast out and that was it.

Every time I went to a family gathering, I was the boy who made it. I was a Professor at Harvard and everybody stood around in awe and listened to my every word, and all I felt was that horror that I knew inside that I didn't know.

I realized that although everything by which I knew myself, even my body and this life itself, was gone, still I was fully aware! Not only that, but this aware "I" was watching the entire drama, including the panic, with calm compassion.

I thought at that moment, "Wow, I've got it made. I'm just a new beautiful being — I'm just an inner self — all I'll ever need to do is look inside and I'll know what to do and I can always trust it, and here I'll be forever."
It was as if the whole western mind-training of individual differences had been made background instead of figure, so that you'd look at another human being and say, "Here we are."

We had a Negro psychiatrist, Madison Presnell, working with us, and I had been trained to be a very liberal person about Negroes, which meant that you didn't have feelings. It was a phony kind of liberal thing.

I recall starting to "come down" and this huge red wave rolled in across the room. … It was all my identities, all rolling in over me. I remember holding up my hand and saying, "NO, NO, I don't want to go back."
We had gotten over the feeling that one experience was going to make you enlightened forever. We saw that it wasn't going to be that simple.
